partners.diseaseBName: growth hormone insensitivity syndrome with immune dysregulation 2, autosomal dominant
partners.mechanism_chain: STAT5B (HGNC:11075) —DISRUPTS→ JAK/STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242); JAK/STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —LEADS_TO→ Immune dysregulation (HP:0002715); JAK/STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —LEADS_TO→ Growth hormone signaling (GO:0007165); GH1 (HGNC:4220) —DISRUPTS→ Growth hormone signaling (GO:0007165); Growth hormone signaling (GO:0007165) —LEADS_TO→ Growth hormone insensitivity (HP:0011214). Loss-of-function mutations in STAT5B disrupt the JAK/STAT signaling pathway, impacting both immune cell function (leading to immune dysregulation) and growth hormone signaling (contributing to growth hormone insensitivity). While GH1 is the primary gene for growth hormone production, STAT5B is a key downstream mediator of GH signaling, and its dysfunction can manifest as growth hormone insensitivity. Thus, STAT5B acts as a convergence point for the molecular defects leading to both diseases.
